title: Twisted Yangians of quasi-split type DI and Drinfeld type current relations
summary: We study the twisted Yangian associated with the quasi-split symmetric pair $(\mathfrak{o}_{2n}, \mathfrak{o}_{n-1}\oplus \mathfrak{o}_{n+1})$ of type DI. Working in the transposed $R$-matrix presentation of arXiv:2607.14692, we show that the generating matrix $S(u)$ admits no Gaussian decomposition. We decompose instead the matrix $\widehat{S}(u) = G\,S(u)$, where $G$ is the constant term of $S(u)$. A chain of quasi-determinantal embeddings lowers the rank within this family of pairs and ends at $(\mathfrak{o}_4,\mathfrak{o}_3)$. Together with a direct study of a degenerate block of type AI, this gives a presentation of the special twisted Yangian $SY^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{o}_{2n},\mathfrak{o}_{n-1}\oplus \mathfrak{o}_{n+1})$ by Drinfeld type current relations. The two fork nodes of the Dynkin diagram carry Drinfeld's presentation of $Y(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. All other relations are those of split type DI, except that the Serre relation with a doubled fork node has zero right hand side. For $n\ge3$ we obtain an explicit isomorphism between the $R$-matrix presentation of Guay and Regelskis and the Drinfeld presentation of Lu and Zhang. The Drinfeld generators are expressed through the Gaussian series of $\widehat{S}(u)$. With quasi-split type AIII (Lu and Zhang), this completes the explicit comparison for the classical quasi-split types with a nontrivial diagram involution.

title: Shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces
summary: We describe the shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces, through their global integrations and their homotopy Poisson algebras. We construct the adjoint symplectic groupoid of the surface explicitly, show that admissible curves integrate to embedded Lagrangian subgroupoids, which are 1-shifted Lagrangians, and characterize when their shifted intersections are clean. For a component of the degeneracy locus, a canonical Hamiltonian flow on its shifted self-intersection recovers the modular period. On the infinitesimal side, the homotopy Poisson algebra of a connected admissible curve not contained in the degeneracy locus is $L_\infty$-isomorphic to its underlying cochain complex, and its $L_\infty$-isomorphism class is determined by the total contact multiplicity. The brackets of arity at least two can be removed by a change of tubular neighbourhood exactly when all contacts are transverse. At tangential contacts, the binary bracket retains the modular vector field. We establish this distinction using a general characterization of the $L_\infty$-isomorphisms induced by changes of tubular neighbourhood, valid for arbitrary coisotropic submanifolds.

title: On minimal singular vectors of $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ for types $B$ and $C$
summary: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra of type $B$ or $C$ over ${\mathbb C}$. Given $κ\in{\mathbb C}$, let $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra associated with $\mathfrak{g}$ at level $κ$. We characterize the weights of minimal singular vectors of $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ with respect to the generalized Cartan matrix, when $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ is not simple and $κ$ is not critical. Furthermore, we determine the corresponding longest Weyl elements in the Kashiwara-Tanisaki character theorem of the singular vectors.

title: Worldsheet skeins and block decomposition of quivers
comment: 46 pages, 5 figures; a Mathematica file is attached as an ancillary file
summary: Following the knot-quiver correspondence, we investigate quiver counterparts of the HOMFLYPT skein relations by interpreting link invariants in terms of holomorphic worldsheets and their multicover contributions. Extending this framework to more general worldsheet geometries, we conjecture that, up to quiver equivalence, the adjacency matrix of the quiver associated with any link in a skein triple admits a block decomposition whose diagonal blocks are quiver adjacency matrices associated with the other two links. We verify this conjecture in numerous examples.

title: Clifford BMW Categories and Conformal Embeddings of Types B C and D
summary: In this paper, we give diagrammatic descriptions of the quantum subgroups coming from conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{g}), \check{h}) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{g}}, 1)$ for $\mathfrak{g}\in \left\{\mathfrak{so}_N, \mathfrak{sp}_{2N}\right\}$, as well as the conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}, 2r) \subset \mathcal{C}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}}, 1)$, extending the techniques of Edie-Michell and Snyder which applied to conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sl}_r, r) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sl}_r}, 1)$. Our main conceptual innovation is the use of fermion condensation to construct a continuous family of planar superalgebras, which we call the Clifford BMW supercategories. The tower of endomorphism algebras, $CW_n(σ, ε)$ is a combination of Birman Wenzl Murakami algebras and Clifford algebras, much in the spirit of the Hecke Clifford algebras. This tower of algebras appears to be new, and already yields some exciting combinatorics.

title: Tangle Invariants Valued in Derived Categories of Sheaves and the Rouquier Complex
summary: We develop effective calculation tools for constructing categorified invariants of tangles and knots, following the work of Cautis and Kamnitzer. These invariants, originally constructed by means of Fourier-Mukai transform functors between derived categories of coherent sheaves on certain iterated flag varieties, can be given an alternative algebraic description by using tilting bundles. We use this method and provide several examples of its application, in the hope of showing its utility to explicit pen-and-paper computations. This tilting-bundle method also allows us to lift the construction from derived to homotopy categories of complexes of modules, reducing the calculation of tangle invariants to a type of categorified matrix algebra, where the matrices in question have maps between their elements and calculations get turbocharged with chain homotopy.

title: Classification and $C_2$-cofiniteness of rational vertex operator algebras generated in low conformal weights
summary: We obtain classification results for rational vertex operator algebras generated in low conformal weights. More precisely, we prove that every rational vertex operator algebra of OZ type strongly generated by its conformal weight two subspace $V_2$ is isomorphic to a finite tensor product of Virasoro minimal models. We also prove that every rational vertex operator algebra of CFT type generated as a vertex algebra by its conformal weight one subspace $V_1$ is isomorphic to a finite tensor product of simple affine vertex operator algebras associated with finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras at positive integral levels. Consequently, Zhu's conjecture that rationality implies $C_2$-cofiniteness holds for both classes, and every such rational vertex operator algebra is regular.

title: Hopf algebra polynomial identities in the Sweedler algebra
comment: 12 pages; the introduction may overlap with arXiv:2404.15868; a small typo was corrected
summary: Using Mac Lane's PROPs, one can introduce multilinear polynomial identities that involve all the operations of a Hopf algebra: the (co)multiplication, the (co)unit and the antipode. We find bases for polynomial identities and calculate their codimensions for the Sweedler algebra, treating it first as an ordinary associative algebra over a field and second as a Hopf algebra.

title: Reflective algebras over factorizable Hopf algebras
summary: The reflective algebra $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$, introduced by Laugwitz, Walton and Yakimov, is a quasitriangular left $H$-comodule algebra constructed from a quasitriangular Hopf algebra $(H,R)$ and a left $H$-comodule algebra $A$. We study the structure and factorizability of finite-dimensional reflective algebras. When $(H,R)$ is factorizable, we show that $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$ is isomorphic, as a quasitriangular left $H$-comodule algebra, to $A\otimes H$ equipped with the trivial left $H$-coaction on $A$ and the universal $K$-matrix induced by $R_{21}R$. In this case, we also classify all universal $K$-matrices on $R_H(A)$. Finally, we prove that $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$ is factorizable if and only if $(H,R)$ is factorizable and $A$ is simple as an algebra.

title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
comment: 11 pages; v2 adds an acknowledgements section, text and mathematical content remain unchanged
summary: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.

title: A diagrammatic presentation for every pivotal pointed fusion category
summary: We provide a generators and relations presentation of pivotal pointed fusion categories, $Vec(G,ω,π)$. Unlike the well-known skeletal model, our presentation is strict and allows multiple isomorphic objects. Our main tool is skein theory, which allows us to apply topological tools to understand the relations of morphisms in the category. This expository paper provides details of skein-theoretic work in the setup that allows multiple isomorphic labels in the generators, which didn't previously exist in the literature.

title: Algebra of the Infrared with Elliptic Curve-Valued Potential
summary: We study an extension of the algebra of the infrared to curve--valued potentials, focusing on the elliptic curve case. Given a finite configuration of points on an elliptic curve, we construct associated \(L_\infty\)-algebra. Adding an extra point produces a directed \(A_\infty\)-algebra and an \(L_\infty\)-morphism to their directed Hochschild deformation complexes. Maurer--Cartan elements of the \(L_\infty\)-algebra determine \(A_\infty\)-deformations of the directed algebra. We formulate a conjectural comparison between Maurer--Cartan deformations of the directed algebra and the directed Fukaya--Seidel category associated to compatible finite collections of thimbles.

title: Modular invariants and NIM-reps
summary: Given a pivotal module category over a spherical fusion category, we introduce the encircling module, a module over the fusion algebra defined using the pivotal structure, and prove that it is isomorphic to the NIM-rep as a fusion algebra module. When applied to the $\mathcal{TM}$ realisation of the modular invariant partition function (arXiv:1911.09024), this identifies the NIM-rep multiplicities with the entries $Z_{I,I^\vee}$ of the modular invariant (its diagonal relative to the charge-conjugation invariant, which is the one given by the regular module category), providing a categorical generalisation of Böckenhauer, Evans and Kawahigashi's results (arXiv:math/9907149). We also show that for indecomposable module categories the dimension condition on $\mathcal{TM}$ required for modular invariance is automatically satisfied, and that $\mathcal{TM}$ is, as an algebra, the full centre of the module category in the sense of Davydov, Kong and Runkel (arXiv:1307.5956), which for module categories of algebras is the full centre of Fjelstad, Fuchs, Runkel and Schweigert (arXiv:hep-th/0612306). Consequently $\mathcal{TM}$ gives rise to Cardy algebras in the sense of Kong and Runkel (arXiv:0807.3356).

title: Quantum Theory Over Dual-Complex Numbers
summary: We take quantum theory and replace C by C[e] where e^2 = 0, i.e. we extend quantum theory to the ring of dual complex numbers. The aim is to develop a common language in which to treat continuous quantum physics and discrete quantum models in a unified manner, including their symmetries. Since quantum theory is linear, introducing e is enough to model infinitesimals. A first objection to this programme is that C[e] is not a field, since division by e is undefined, while quantum mechanics typically relies on division. A second objection concerns whether unitarity still makes sense given e^2 = 0. Hence, the core of this work is dedicated to proving that dual-complex quantum theory remains fully consistent. In particular, norm is preserved at all times, and renormalization never requires dividing by an infinitesimal. An equivalence with conventional quantum theory is demonstrated: the dual-complex extension of a parametrized quantum operation automatically provides a linear treatment of its first-order variations. As a first example application, we provide a unified description of both the Dirac equation in the continuum and the Dirac Quantum Walk in the discrete. We establish the discrete Lorentz covariance of the latter.

title: On singular vectors and associated Weyl elements for simply-laced universal affine vertex operator algebras
comment: Corrected title metadata and added author affiliations and email addresses. Mathematical content unchanged. 53 pages
summary: Given a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and a complex number $κ$, let $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ be the associated universal affine vertex algebra. Gorelik and Kac [GK07] gave a sufficient and necessary condition for $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ to be simple. In this paper, for simply-laced $\mathfrak{g}$ and non-critical $κ$, we determine the weights of singular vectors of $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ with minimal conformal weights, when $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ is not simple. We further determine all the longest Weyl elements in the Kashiwara-Tanisaki character theorem [KT00] which correspond to the weights of the singular vectors.

title: Higher path groupoids and the holonomy of formal power series connections
comment: 22 pages. v2: added more examples, more general formulation of formal power series connections in terms of algebras instead of coalgebras, added details to final section, corrected typos
summary: Building on ideas of Kohno, we develop a framework for the construction of higher holonomy functors via the transport of formal power series connections. Using these techniques, we obtain functors from the path groupoid, the path 2-groupoid, and the path 3-groupoid of a manifold. We show that the resulting higher holonomy functors can detect non-trivial classes in higher homotopy groups. As an application, we construct a Gray functor from the path 3-groupoid of the configuration space of $m$ points in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $n\geqslant 4$ and compute its restriction to 3-tracks with constant boundary when $n=4$.
